paragraphs: R' Chiyya son of Rav Yeiva, [Sukkah 42b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.42b.2).
Rav Chanin son of Rav Yeiva, [Bava Batra 174a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.174a.11-12).

Rav Sama son of Rav Yeiva, [Bava Batra 9a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.9a.11); Dikdukei Soferim reads Rav Safra, as does [Bava Batra 5a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.5a.4). Rami son of Rav Yeiva, [Shabbat 83a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.83a.6).
Rav Shmuel bar Yeiva, [Niddah 15b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.15b.5). But almost all of them lived in different times.[^2][^3]

notes.text: The Sama/Safra reading is Hyman’s reported variant. This is a collective list: Hyman expressly says that almost all these figures lived at different times.

Sukkah reads Rav Chiyya. In Bava Batra 9a, Sama addresses Rav Papa about a poor man’s request. Bava Batra 5a names Safra in a different account with Ravina. The parallel patronymics belong to distinct notices.
The linked passage names Rav Acha son of Rav Yeiva transmitting a ruling in Mar Zutra’s name.
